text:
anya: heads up — on the babel-bridge bring-up I’m seeing a weird BLEU drop for zh↔en after the qint8 + kvcache change. Repro on our small testset: baseline 34.6 -> qint8 30.2. :thinking:
cheng: ugh that's large. Any examples? tokenization or detok mismatch?
anya: short example: input: "江苏科技大学（分校）在2019年举办的研讨会。"
anya: baseline detok: 江苏科技大学（分校）在 2019 年举办的研讨会。
anya: qint8 detok: 江苏科技大学（分校）在2019年举办的 研讨会。
anya: difference is spacing around numbers and CJK punctuation — seems like token boundaries moved which breaks our BLEU scoring and some model outputs change.
jun: can you paste the tokenized ids before/after? maybe the tokenizer changed or byte fallback kicked in.
anya: before: [5021, 3012, 9987, 409, 111, 2233]
anya: after:  [5021, 3012, 9987, 409111, 2233]  <-- note merged 409+111 into single token id 409111 (example)
anya: that merged token is why attention and kvcache alignment shift.
cheng: is this specific to that input or systemic? run the qa suite with 1000 zh samples?
anya: kicking off now with eval-bot. cc @sam for infra flags (maybe kernel selection changed on the int8 build). :eyes:

eval-bot: running eval suite: babel-bridge qint8-kvcache vs baseline
eval-bot: 1000 zh-en samples completed — BLEU delta = -3.8, regression concentrated on numeric/punctuation group (45% of regressions)
eval-bot: top failure patterns: merged CJK+number tokens, bracket orientation with RTL punctuation, and unexpected ZWJ merges.
sam: that sounds like a tokenization fallback/serialization edge. Did the model vocab or tokenizer package bump in the build? Any pip/packaging diffs?
jun: checking build diff — tokenizers==0.12.1 -> 0.12.3, plus hash change in tokenizer-config.json in model bundle. Possibly new token merge rules.
cheng: can we bisect: quantization vs tokenizer change vs runtime kernel? propose: 1) run baseline weights + new tokenizer 2) new weights + old tokenizer 3) qint8 runtime w/old tokenizer. helps isolate.
anya: started (1) & (2) jobs on canary.
anya: quick sanity commands I used: ```
# tokenize sample
python -c "from tokenizers import Tokenizer; t=Tokenizer.from_file('tok.json'); print(t.encode('江苏科技大学（分校）在2019年举办的研讨会。').tokens)"
```
anya: output differs per tok.json variant.

sam: pinging infra to ensure we didn't flip kernel selection for qint8 on canary GPUs. Also check kernel-level padding/align path that could affect K/V cache indexing.

jun: FYI I found a deterministic repro where token merge occurs only when kv-cache chunking enabled (batching param >1). So maybe prefix caching interacts with tokenizer normalization step in our preprocessing pipeline.

anya: nice find. I'll run a focused test (single vs batched) and attach logs. If tokenizer change caused this it's a release roll-back candidate; if runtime bug then we need a quick patch.

cheng: thanks — if anyone sees the same pattern on ja/ko or mixed scripts, flag it here. I'll start a small bisect matrix and post links to runs. :thumbsup:
